context_menu.label: Show the current function body again

menu.reconcile_note: The original body is need-more-context on its own: it decodes the Authorization header, then defers accept/deny to two callees. Delivering both on-target bodies resolves it. httpPwdDecode (0x4450c8) shows the credential is base64-decoded from the request and split at ':', so the accepted string comes from request input, not from any literal in the body. httpGenListFind (0x43fb60) shows that decoded credential is length-checked then strcmp-matched against the provisioned stored-user list, so acceptance is delegated to external configuration state. Together they prove the gate grants only on an exact match to an externally provisioned account, which is not-vulnerable. The same two bodies do not fix either mutant, because each mutant's flaw sits inside httpRpmPass's own body: M1 adds a branch that accepts the raw header 'Basic YWRtaW46dHBsMzM3' (base64 admin:tpl337) and returns success before the list walk ever runs, and M8 sprintf's the attacker-controlled decoded credential into a 256-byte stack buffer and hands it to a printf/exec-family sink. The callees resolve the original but cannot override an in-body bypass or sink, so each mutant stays vulnerable under this identical menu. The three off-target items are real same-binary callees off the accept/deny path (base64 primitive, header reader, buffer allocator) and add nothing to the verdict.

mutants.relabel_v3_1: 2026-10-06: relabeled vulnerable -> not-vulnerable (gpu-setup + user decision). The backdoor branch matches 'Basic YWRtaW46dHBsMzM3' but only calls 0x496aec (realm header) and returns 0; it never sets REMOTE_USER (-0x71b4) and never calls the grant (-0x72ec), so the match does not open access. 0/24 solved. Flip group keeps its vulnerable pole via M8.
